content: Academics have to invest tremendous effort into a single paper, so we often work on papers that we suspect will yield interesting & significant results. But that also pushes us to predictable work. AI has no such constraints, forcing us to rethink a lot of how science is done. New working paper: Can AI forecast treatment effects in economics from pre-registration documents? Answer: Yes. 1/

Recommended read. One of my favourite research topics in the last year. Learning from raw bytes and the potential efficiency gains. The crazy part is that this is just scratching the surface. I've always believed that intelligence should come from simple, general building blocks that learn their own abstractions directly from raw data; in other words, the bitter lesson. I think we're finally seeing a real step towards AI that can learn from all data. Language modelin…
